is_anopheles.evidence: The study investigates Anopheles gambiae s.l. (specifically identified as Anopheles gambiae s.s. and Anopheles coluzzii) alongside Aedes aegypti and Culex quinquefasciatus (page 1, Abstract; page 9, 'Mutations in Anopheles gambiae s.l.').

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper genotypes Vgsc L1014F (L995F) and L1014S (L995S) in Anopheles gambiae s.s. and Anopheles coluzzii (page 6, Table 2; page 10, Table 5).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 5 (page 10) reports exact genotype counts (RR, RS, SS) and sample sizes for both L1014F and L1014S across 38 Anopheles gambiae s.s. and 106 Anopheles coluzzii specimens.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquito larvae were collected from field breeding sites at the Port of Cotonou, Benin, and reared to F1 adults for testing (pages 3-5, 'Larval collection methods' and 'Larval collection from breeding sites').

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary research study presenting original bioassay and molecular resistance data collected between 2023 and 2024.

sub_country_location.evidence: Collections were conducted at specific georeferenced sites within the Port of Cotonou, Cotonou, Benin (page 3, Figure 1).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected between June 2023 and November 2024 (page 1, Abstract; page 3, 'Methods').

duplicate_risk.evidence: While the text notes that larval collection 'was part of a larger study carried out from June 2023 to May 2024 at the Port of Cotonou' (page 3), these are original primary field surveillance data presented for the first time.

supplement.evidence: All relevant Anopheles sample sizes and kdr genotype counts are fully reported in Table 5 of the main text.

assessment.summary: This study evaluated insecticide susceptibility and resistance markers in mosquitoes from the Port of Cotonou, Benin. In Anopheles gambiae s.s. (n = 38) and Anopheles coluzzii (n = 106) surviving pyrethroid bioassays, kdr L1014F (Vgsc L995F) was found at high frequencies (f = 0.8421 and 0.9292, respectively), while L1014S (Vgsc L995S) was detected only in heterozygous An. gambiae s.s. (f = 0.052).
